problem: “We have an idea, but we don’t know if it’s a business.”
solution: A feasibility study that sizes the market, maps the competition and models unit economics, so you decide on evidence rather than optimism.

problem: “Our bank asked for a business plan we don’t have.”
solution: A lender-ready plan with defensible projections, use of funds and a narrative that answers underwriting questions before they’re asked.

problem: “We’re launching and nothing is set up yet.”
solution: An operations-setup roadmap covering entity and registration checklist, banking, tools, vendors and back office, sequenced so nothing is missed.

problem: “We look smaller than we are.”
solution: Brand foundations, capability statements and pitch materials that give a young company the presence of an established one.

problem: “We don’t know who to sell to first.”
solution: Ideal-customer definition, offer design and a first-90-days go-to-market plan with clear weekly actions.

problem: “We need investors to take us seriously.”
solution: A tight investor narrative, financial model and data room checklist, rehearsed until the story holds up to hard questions.

problem: “Our pipeline is feast or famine.”
solution: A sales operating system covering segmented target lists, scripts, follow-up cadences, CRM stages and a weekly scorecard that makes revenue predictable.

problem: “Customers can’t find us on Google.”
solution: Technical, on-page and local SEO implementation: site fixes, structured data, Google Business Profile and content that matches how buyers search.

problem: “Our marketing is random acts of activity.”
solution: Positioning, messaging and a channel plan sized to your budget, with the few metrics that prove what’s working.

problem: “We get referrals, but only by luck.”
solution: A structured referral-partner program, with partner collateral, a sharing cadence and tracking, so introductions become a channel.

problem: “Our CRM is a graveyard.”
solution: CRM cleanup and redesign: pipeline stages, required fields, automations and a hygiene routine your team will actually follow.

problem: “Our sales materials don’t match our quality.”
solution: Collateral systems (brochures, one-pagers, case studies, proposals) designed to a consistent, premium standard.

problem: “Everything runs through the owner.”
solution: Documented SOPs, clear decision rights and an operating rhythm that lets the business run without you in every room.

problem: “Our projects always run late and over budget.”
solution: Project management discipline, with scoping, schedules, budgets, risk logs and status reporting, applied to your critical initiatives.

problem: “We’re drowning in admin.”
solution: Back-office redesign covering vendor management, compliance calendars, document control and delegation, with the busywork automated where possible.

problem: “We don’t know our numbers until it’s too late.”
solution: A weekly KPI dashboard built on the handful of numbers that actually drive the business, updated without manual effort.

problem: “New hires take months to get useful.”
solution: Onboarding playbooks, role scorecards and training plans that cut ramp-up time and make expectations explicit.

problem: “Leadership meetings go nowhere.”
solution: A meeting cadence with scorecards, issue lists and accountability, so decisions get made and stay made.

problem: “We know AI could help, but where do we start?”
solution: A workflow audit that finds the repetitive, high-volume work, then a scoped first AI project with guardrails, measured in hours saved.

problem: “Our website embarrasses us.”
solution: A fast, elegant, accessible website engineered for search and conversion, one you can update yourself.

problem: “We re-type the same data into five systems.”
solution: Workflow automation connecting forms, CRM, spreadsheets and email, so information is entered once and flows everywhere.

problem: “We pay for software nobody uses.”
solution: A technology stack review that rationalizes tools, recovers spend and gets the remaining systems properly adopted.

problem: “Our files and accounts are a security risk.”
solution: Workspace setup, access controls, password management and backup basics, documented and handed over.

problem: “Reports take days to put together.”
solution: Clean data structures and automated dashboards that answer the real business questions on demand.

problem: “We know grants exist, but not which ones fit.”
solution: Funding research that produces a prioritized pipeline of grants and programs matched to your mission, with deadlines and go/no-go calls.

problem: “Our last grant application was rejected.”
solution: A readiness review and rewritten application with a sharper project, a defensible budget, measurable outcomes and stronger evidence.

problem: “We need to hire, but cash flow is tight.”
solution: Navigation of workforce programs such as on-the-job training and work-based learning reimbursements, matched to your hiring plan.

problem: “We’re not registered to receive federal funds.”
solution: A registration and compliance checklist (SAM.gov, UEI and program-specific portals), handled methodically and early.

problem: “Government RFPs are overwhelming.”
solution: Capability statements, compliance matrices and proposal writing for public and private procurement.

problem: “We won the grant. Now what?”
solution: Post-award systems covering expense tracking, outcome reporting and audit-ready records, so you’re fundable again next cycle.

problem: “We need a COO but can’t justify a full-time hire.”
solution: Fractional operating leadership: senior ownership of agreed objectives for the days each month that matter most.

problem: “Our big initiative keeps slipping.”
solution: An accountable leader who owns the initiative end to end, with a plan, a team rhythm and visible progress.

problem: “We’re between leaders.”
solution: Interim leadership that keeps momentum and morale steady through a transition, then hands over cleanly.

problem: “I have no one to think out loud with.”
solution: Strategic advisory: a trusted, candid sounding board for owners making high-stakes decisions.

problem: “We tried to hire a senior leader and it failed.”
solution: Build the function fractionally first, then define, recruit and onboard the right permanent hire into a role that’s proven.

problem: “Sales and operations don’t talk to each other.”
solution: Cross-functional strategic operations that align targets, handoffs and reporting across the business.

problem: “We have a medical device concept and a blank page.”
solution: Ground-up R&D planning covering problem definition, user needs, prior-art and literature landscape, concept options and a staged development roadmap.

problem: “Our formulation works in theory, not yet in the lab.”
solution: Formulation research planning: ingredient and excipient review, design-of-experiments, stability considerations and lab-partner coordination.

problem: “We don’t know which FDA pathway applies to us.”
solution: Regulatory pathway research covering device classification, predicate landscape and likely routes, organized so your regulatory counsel starts ahead.

problem: “We need prototypes but don’t know who can make them.”
solution: Materials, supplier and contract-manufacturer sourcing, with specifications and quotes managed to a plan.

problem: “Research is expensive and we’re pre-revenue.”
solution: Non-dilutive funding strategy for innovators, including SBIR/STTR and research grants, aligned to your development milestones.

problem: “Our R&D lives in notebooks and inboxes.”
solution: Documentation habits and research records structured from day one, the foundation for design controls and investor diligence.

problem: “Our books don’t reconcile and nobody knows why.”
solution: Forensic bookkeeping that rebuilds the records, traces transactions and pinpoints where and why the numbers diverge.

problem: “We think money is leaking somewhere.”
solution: A leakage review covering unbilled work, duplicate payments, unapplied credits, vendor overcharges and misclassified costs, with findings ranked by dollar impact.

problem: “We may be missing credits or incentives we qualify for.”
solution: A credits-and-incentives review that surfaces potential tax credits, incentives, reimbursements and certifications, and coordinates with your CPA to claim them.

problem: “Years of records are a mess before a sale, loan or audit.”
solution: Financial reconstruction: organized, reconciled, documented records your CPA, lender or buyer can rely on.

problem: “Our project is stuck in permits and approvals.”
solution: Entitlements coordination that maps the approvals, requirements and stakeholders, and keeps the process moving with the right professionals.

problem: “We qualify for certifications but never applied.”
solution: Small-business certification readiness (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, DBE, SDVOSB and state programs) to open doors to set-aside work.
